segments.t: 50 basis point hike if CPI inflation hit .3 for the month, which I didn't think it was
going to, but it did.
And that's the third straight month in a row.
The average annualized out, that's heading for 3.5%, not getting closer to two.
So I think that's where we need a more aggressive approach.
Now people have argued to you 50 in December, nothing in January, or 25 in December, 25
in January.
In a normal world, they're kind of the same.
But when you do 25 now and you're going to do 25 in January, it only affects market pricing.
If you signal, you're going to do it.
And you give the markets a credible signal that, hey, we're going to go again in January.
But if we don't signal that, and we just raise the rate 25 basis points in December,
and then the markets are like, are they going to go again?
Maybe they're not going to go again.
We don't get that market effect.
So in that world, if you're not going to signal this very clearly to markets, you're going
in January, my view is then you have to go 50 in December to put it in place and get
it done.
It sounds like you're saying the Fed is sort of hobbling itself to this new way of not
really using forward guidance from either the chair or from the statement.
Well, I think there's other ways you can do it.
Like the SEP in September was clearly signaling two or three hikes going forward in the next
couple of months.
And the markets priced that in.
This SEP that's coming out in December is not going to be that useful because it's going
to ask us what is the rate at the end of 27.
It doesn't tell you anything about January, March, early half of the year.
You could have it go up and then come down the second half of the year.
So the SEP is not going to provide the signaling that it did in September.
And so we're going to have to try to use other ways to get that signal across.
But it's not, could it be in the statement?
Because one of the things that's happened is the statement has been boiled down to,
I guess, under 130 words or around 130 words.
I mean, you certainly could put some language that signals that.
The chair could actually talk about it if you wanted to.
